note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: You are asked to test a newly wired distribution board with six circuits. What should you do before you take any readings?
options: Switch the main breaker on so each circuit can be tried
Start with whichever circuit is nearest to the door
Get the drawings, plan the test order, check instruments
Ask the customer which of the tests they would like skipped

questions.stem: Which instrument is best for proving that a circuit is dead before you work on it?
options: A two-pole voltage indicator checked on a proving unit
A non-contact voltage pen held next to the cable
A digital multimeter left on its resistance setting
A neon screwdriver touched on the line terminal

questions.stem: Why is the voltage indicator checked on a known source both before and after you test a circuit for dead?
options: To warm up the tester so its readings are more accurate
To use up the old battery charge before the next job
To check that the circuit has not come back on by itself
To prove the tester did not fail during the test

questions.stem: Which measurement category is meant for work at the origin of an installation, such as the service entrance?
options: CAT II
CAT IV
CAT I
CAT III

questions.stem: For testing inside a distribution board, you can choose a meter marked CAT III 600 V or one marked CAT II 1000 V. Which is better, and why?
options: CAT II 1000 V, because a higher voltage is always safer
CAT III 600 V, because its category suits a distribution board
Either one, because the board only has 220 V in it
CAT II 1000 V, because categories only matter for DC work

questions.stem: Which test probes are best for work in a distribution board?
options: Probes with long bare metal tips that reach deep terminals
Probes repaired with tape where the insulation has split
Crocodile clips fitted to long leads with no fuses in them
Probes with finger guards, short tips and fused leads

questions.stem: A high-impedance digital meter shows 40 V on a cable that has been isolated, but a two-pole tester shows nothing. What is the most likely cause?
options: Voltage picked up from live cables running beside it
The breaker is faulty and is still feeding the cable
The meter's battery is low, so it shows a random number
The cable has a short circuit between line and neutral

questions.stem: What does the low-impedance (LoZ) setting on some meters help you to do?
options: Measure very small resistances in the protective conductors
Measure currents above 10 A without using a clamp
Tell a real voltage from one picked up from nearby cables
Test insulation resistance at a lower test voltage

questions.stem: Why should a true-RMS meter be used to measure the current drawn by a variable-speed drive or LED lighting?
options: Because these loads only work on direct current
Because other meters cannot measure more than 1 A
Because these loads draw no current when they start
Because their current is not a clean sine wave

questions.stem: A meter's accuracy is ±(1% of reading + 2 digits). It shows 220.0 V on a range that reads to 0.1 V. Between which limits could the true voltage be?
What is the difference between a meter's resolution and its accuracy?
options: Resolution is the smallest step shown; accuracy is how near to the true value
Resolution is how near to the true value; accuracy is the smallest step shown
Resolution is the highest reading; accuracy is the lowest reading
They mean the same thing and are given together as one figure

questions.stem: Why does a voltmeter need a very high internal resistance?
options: So that it can safely carry the full load current of the circuit
So that the battery inside lasts for many years
So it draws almost no current and does not upset the circuit
So that it can be connected in series with the load

questions.stem: Why does a meter's current range have a very low internal resistance?
options: So that it shows the supply voltage at the same time
So that it can be connected straight across the supply
So that it adds almost nothing to the circuit's resistance
So that it protects the circuit in just the way a fuse would

questions.stem: A 3½-digit meter can show up to 1999 on its display. On its 200 V range, what is the smallest step it can show?
options: 1 V

questions.stem: Before an insulation test on a lighting circuit, the dimmer and the LED drivers cannot be removed. What should you do?
options: Test at the highest voltage the tester can give
Join line and neutral together and test them to earth
Test between line and neutral only, with the drivers in
Leave the circuit live so the drivers are not stressed

questions.stem: After an insulation test on a long cable, why must you wait before touching the conductors?
options: The cable is hot from the test current
The tester must cool down fully before the next reading
The insulation takes time to dry out after a test
The cable can hold a charge until the tester drains it

questions.stem: Insulation readings on five circuits are 200 MΩ, 150 MΩ, 180 MΩ, 0.4 MΩ and 220 MΩ. What should you do about the 0.4 MΩ circuit?
options: Treat it as suspect, find the cause and retest it
Accept it, because the other four circuits are very good
Switch it on and see if the breaker trips under load
Average the five readings and accept them together

questions.stem: Why do you null (zero) the test leads before measuring the resistance of a protective conductor?
options: To charge up the capacitors inside the tester before use
To check the battery is fully charged
To set the tester to its highest range
To take the leads' own resistance out of the result

questions.stem: On a radial circuit, you link the line and protective conductors at the board and measure between them at the far outlet. What does this reading give you?
options: The insulation resistance between line and earth
The resistance of line plus protective conductor, end to end
The current the circuit will draw at full load
The voltage drop on the circuit at full load

questions.stem: Why is a polarity test done on every single-pole switch and lamp holder?
options: To check that the lamp will give its full brightness
To make sure the neutral is switched and not the line
To make sure the switch breaks the line conductor
To check that the earth carries the load current

questions.stem: In an earth electrode test with two test spikes, why are readings taken with the middle spike in three positions?
options: To charge the soil so that the next reading is lower
To find the deepest point that the rod has reached
To measure the current flowing in the building's earth wire
To check the readings agree, so the result can be trusted

questions.stem: Before testing the resistance of an earth rod on its own, what must be done with the installation?
options: Leave it working so the earth carries some current
Pour water round the rod first so that it gives a better result
Isolate it, then disconnect the earth conductor from the rod
Join the rod to the neutral so they share the test

questions.stem: A competent person finds that an earth fault loop impedance reading is much higher than the designer allowed. Why is this a danger?
options: A fault may not trip the protection fast enough
The circuit's insulation will fail at the next test
The lamps on the circuit will glow much brighter
The breaker will trip every time the load starts

questions.stem: Why should an RCD or GFCI be tested with an RCD tester as well as with its own test button?
options: The button test also checks the earth rod's resistance to earth
The tester measures trip time; the button only shows it trips
The button test works only when the circuit is dead
The tester resets the device so it can be used again

questions.stem: Some tests, such as loop impedance and RCD trip time, can only be done with the supply on. Which is the right approach?
options: Any trainee may do them, as long as they wear gloves
Only a competent person does them, with the right tester and rules
They are done with the panel cover off so all terminals can be reached
They are done after removing the main earth to get a clearer reading

questions.stem: A leakage clamp placed around both the line and the neutral of a circuit reads 8 mA. What does this show?
options: About 8 mA is escaping by another path, such as earth
The circuit's total load current is only 8 mA
The neutral is carrying 8 mA more than the earth
The meter is faulty, as the reading should be the load

questions.stem: A small current is hard to read on a clamp meter, so you wind the conductor through the jaws 5 times. The meter reads 4.0 A. What is the real current?
options: 9 A

questions.stem: An oscilloscope is set to 5 ms per division, and one full cycle of a waveform takes 4 divisions. What is its frequency?
options: 20 Hz
200 Hz
50 Hz
5 Hz

questions.stem: When is a phase rotation (phase sequence) tester used?
options: To check that a single-phase socket is wired correctly
To measure how fast a motor's shaft is turning
To check the order of the three phases before a motor is connected
To test the insulation between the three phases

questions.stem: Why must a thermal camera survey of a distribution board be done while the circuits carry their normal load?
options: The camera needs mains power from the board to work
Cold terminals cannot be seen by the camera at all
Load current stops the camera's lens from misting
A loose joint only heats up when current flows

questions.stem: On a 24 V training circuit with the switch on, you measure 24 V across the two terminals of the switch, and the lamp is off. What does this show?
options: The switch is working normally
The switch contacts are not making contact
The lamp is short-circuited
The neutral is connected to earth

questions.stem: A 24 V training circuit works, but one terminal gets warm. With the load on, you measure 1.5 V across that one joint. What does this show?
options: The joint has extra resistance and must be remade
The joint is good, because the lamp still lights
The supply voltage is too high for the circuit
The cable is too large for the terminal

questions.stem: You must measure the resistance of a 2.5 mm² protective conductor about 20 m long. Which instrument gives the most useful reading?
options: A low-resistance ohmmeter that reads to 0.01 Ω
A multimeter on its 20 MΩ resistance range
An insulation tester set to 500 V
A clamp meter on its lowest current range

questions.stem: A meter's calibration certificate ran out last month, and a big test job starts tomorrow. What should the team leader do?
options: Use it anyway, since it was accurate last month
Use an in-date meter and send this one for calibration
Check it on one socket outlet and carry on with it
Use it, but write the results in pencil only

questions.stem: Between calibrations, how can you check that an insulation and continuity tester is still reading correctly?
options: Compare it with the reading on the customer's energy meter
Test it on the same socket outlet every morning
Test it on a check box of known resistances and log it
Shake it gently and see if the display settles

questions.stem: On a schedule of test results, why is each reading written against its circuit number and the instrument's serial number?
options: So the readings can be added up to a total for the board
So the customer can see which tester cost the most
So the tester's battery life can be worked out later
So any reading can be traced and checked again later

questions.stem: Line plus protective conductor reads 0.9 Ω on a 30 m circuit. The same cable on a 15 m circuit reads 0.22 Ω. What should you suspect on the 30 m circuit?
options: Nothing; longer circuits always read about four times as high
The insulation is breaking down between the conductors
The 15 m reading must be wrong, because it is too low
A loose or poor joint, as it is about double the expected

questions.stem: Which instrument shows the true power in watts and the power factor of a running machine?
options: A continuity tester
An insulation resistance tester
A power analyser (or wattmeter)
A phase rotation tester

questions.stem: As team leader, you see a trainee about to test an outlet with a meter whose leads are cracked. What should you do?
options: Stop the test, take the leads out of use and report them
Let the test go ahead, as the trainee is wearing gloves
Tell them to wrap tape on the cracks and continue
Let them finish, then talk about it at the end of the day

questions.stem: A multimeter's current-range fuse has blown. What should replace it?
options: Any fuse that fits the holder, to save time
A fuse of the type and rating the maker states
A piece of wire, so the fuse cannot blow again
A higher-rated fuse, so it lasts longer next time

questions.stem: In a busy office, which instrument is best for finding which breaker feeds a socket outlet without switching off the whole board?
options: An insulation resistance tester
A circuit (breaker) finder with a plug-in sender
A phase rotation tester
An earth electrode tester

questions.stem: Why should every switch on a lighting circuit be closed for an insulation test?
options: So that the lamps light up to show the test is working
So that the test current is shared by all of the lamps
So that the tester's battery is not drained too fast
So that the wiring beyond each switch is also tested

questions.stem: Two team members get different readings for the same earth rod. What is the best next step?
options: Use the lower reading, since it looks better
Average the two and write that down as the result
Check both methods and instruments, then repeat the test
Report the higher reading and stop testing

questions.stem: After locking off a breaker and proving the circuit dead, you leave the site for an hour. What should you do when you return?
options: Test for dead again before touching any conductor
Carry on, since the lock is still on the breaker
Switch the breaker on and off to check that it works
Ask someone else whether anyone touched the board

questions.stem: Your tests find a circuit that fails. The customer wants it switched on today. What should you do?
options: Switch it on and note the fault on the invoice
Leave it isolated, label it and report the fault in writing
Switch it on, but only if the breaker does not trip straight away
Remove the earth wire so the fault does not trip it

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Which measurement category (CAT) is meant for distribution boards and fixed wiring inside a building?
What is the name of the device that gives a known voltage to check a voltage indicator, without using a live circuit?
What type of meter measures alternating current correctly even when it is not a clean sine wave?
What do the letters RMS stand for, when describing an AC voltage or current?
A 10 : 1 oscilloscope probe is used, and the screen shows 3 V. What is the real voltage at the probe tip, in volts?
What type of tester measures the resistance between an earth rod and the general mass of the earth?
A meter shows 0.215 kV. What is this in volts?
Which instrument draws a graph of voltage against time on a screen?
What resistance, in ohms, would you expect for 40 m of conductor at 0.012 Ω per metre?
A meter's accuracy is ±2% of reading. It reads 50.0 V. What is the largest possible error, in volts?
What name is given to a voltage that a high-impedance meter shows on a dead cable because of live cables nearby?
What is the name of the record sheet on which each circuit's test readings are written?
An RCD tester measures how long the device takes to open after a fault current is applied. What is this time called?
Which document gives an instrument's ranges, accuracy and safe use?
A trainee measures 1.12 MΩ. Write this in kilohms.

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and carry out the dead tests on a newly wired distribution board with six final circuits, before it is switched on for the first time. Give the order of the tests and say why the order matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I get the drawings and circuit list, check that my instruments are in calibration and working, and isolate, lock off, tag and prove the board dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after. I inspect the work before testing: terminations tight, cables supported, right breaker sizes, no damage. Then I test in order. First, continuity of the protective conductors (line plus protective conductor for each circuit), so I know the earth path is sound. Second, insulation resistance at the right test voltage, with electronics disconnected or line and neutral joined, so I know there is no fault between conductors or to earth. Third, polarity, so every switch and breaker is in the line. If there is an earth rod, I test it too. Only when all dead tests pass may a competent person switch on and do the live tests. The order matters because a broken earth or failed insulation must be found before any voltage is applied.
markingPoints: Prepares: drawings, instruments in calibration, safe isolation with proved tester
Inspects before testing
Continuity of protective conductors first
Insulation resistance next, protecting electronics; then polarity
Explains that faults must be found before voltage is applied; live tests only by a competent person afterwards

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would safely isolate a 220 V circuit and prove it dead before work, and explain why each step matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I identify the right circuit from the drawings and labels, and tell people in the area. I switch off the breaker or isolator for that circuit, so no current can flow. I fit my own lock and a tag with my name and the date, so nobody can switch it back on while I work. I check my two-pole voltage indicator on a proving unit to make sure it works. Then I test between every pair of conductors at the point of work: line to neutral, line to earth and neutral to earth, because a fault or a wrong label could leave any one of them live. I then check the tester on the proving unit again, to prove it did not fail during the test. Only then do I treat the circuit as dead. If I leave and come back, I test again. I never work live.
markingPoints: Identifies the circuit and warns others
Switches off, locks off and tags
Checks the tester on a proving unit before the test
Tests all conductor pairs at the point of work
Checks the tester again afterwards; never works live

essays.stem: You are buying a multimeter for a team that does installation and maintenance work on 110/220 V systems. Explain what features you would look for and why each matters.
essays.modelAnswer: The meter must have a measurement category that suits where it will be used: at least CAT III for distribution boards and fixed wiring, and CAT IV if it will be used near the supply intake, at a voltage at least as high as the system. This means it can survive voltage spikes without exploding. It should be true RMS, because many loads such as drives, computers and LED drivers draw currents that are not clean sine waves. A low-impedance setting helps tell real voltages from ghost voltages. Its accuracy and resolution should be good enough for the job, and it should have fused current ranges and good-quality leads with finger guards and short exposed tips. A clear display, auto-ranging, a strong case and good battery life help on site. It should come with a calibration certificate, and the maker's instructions should be read before use.
markingPoints: Suitable CAT rating and voltage for the work
True RMS for distorted waveforms
Low-impedance (LoZ) mode or other way to spot ghost voltages
Accuracy, resolution and fused ranges suitable for the job
Safe leads and probes; calibration certificate and maker's instructions

essays.stem: Explain how you would carry out an insulation resistance test on an isolated 220 V circuit that has LED drivers and a surge protector connected, and how you would judge the results.
essays.modelAnswer: I isolate, lock off, tag and prove the circuit dead. I check the tester on its own leads and on a check box. Electronic items such as LED drivers and surge protectors can be damaged by the test voltage or give false low readings, so I disconnect them where possible. Where I cannot, I join line and neutral together and test from them to earth, so there is no test voltage across the electronics. I close all switches so the whole circuit is tested. I test at the usual 500 V DC between line and neutral (if the electronics are out), line and earth, and neutral and earth. After each test I let the tester discharge the cable before touching anything. I compare the readings with the minimum in the specification. A good circuit usually reads very high; a low reading, or one much lower than similar circuits, must be investigated. I record every reading and reconnect everything afterwards.
markingPoints: Safe isolation and tester checked first
Disconnects electronics or links line and neutral to test to earth
Closes switches and tests the right pairs at the usual test voltage
Lets the cable discharge before touching
Compares with the specification, investigates low readings, records and reconnects

essays.stem: A trainee measures 60 V with a digital multimeter on a cable that was isolated and should be dead. Explain what might cause this, how you would find out whether it is real, and what you would do in the meantime.
essays.modelAnswer: The reading may be a ghost voltage. A digital multimeter has a very high input resistance, so it can show a voltage picked up from live cables running in the same conduit or trunking, even though there is almost no energy behind it. But it could also be a real voltage: the wrong breaker may have been switched off, the cable may be fed from a second source, or there may be a borrowed neutral. Until we know, the cable must be treated as live and nobody touches it. To find out, I would test with a two-pole voltage indicator checked on a proving unit, or switch the meter to its low-impedance setting, which loads the cable so a ghost voltage collapses. If the voltage stays, it is real: I would trace the circuit, find the other supply, isolate and lock it off, and test again. I would report it, because a mislabelled board is a danger to others.
markingPoints: Explains ghost voltage from high meter impedance and nearby live cables
Says it could be real (wrong breaker, second supply, borrowed neutral)
Treats the cable as live until proven
Confirms with a two-pole tester or LoZ setting
If real: trace, isolate the source, retest and report

essays.stem: A meter's accuracy is ±(0.5% of reading + 3 digits) on a range that reads to 0.01 V. It shows 12.00 V. Work out the limits of the true value, and explain why accuracy matters when a reading is close to a pass or fail limit.
essays.modelAnswer: 0.5% of 12.00 V is 0.06 V. Three digits on a range that reads to 0.01 V is 0.03 V. The total possible error is 0.06 + 0.03 = 0.09 V. So the true voltage could be anywhere from 11.91 V to 12.09 V. This matters when a result is close to a limit. For example, if a test must show no more than a certain value and the reading is just under it, the true value could be over the limit once the meter's error is counted. In that case I would not simply pass it. I would retest with a more accurate, recently calibrated instrument, or treat the result as doubtful and investigate. Accuracy also matters when comparing readings from two meters: a small difference may only be the meters' errors, not a real change. Knowing the error stops me from passing unsafe work or failing good work.
markingPoints: 0.06 V from the percentage worked correctly
0.03 V from the digits worked correctly
Limits 11.91 V to 12.09 V
Explains the risk of a reading close to a limit
Says what to do: retest with a better instrument or treat as doubtful

essays.stem: Describe how you would test the resistance of a building's earth rod with an earth electrode tester and two test spikes, and how you would record and judge the result.
essays.modelAnswer: I plan the test with the supervisor, because the installation must be isolated before the earth conductor is taken off the rod. I isolate, lock off and prove dead. Then I disconnect the earthing conductor at the rod's test point, so the reading is for the rod alone. I drive the current spike well away from the rod, and the potential spike in a straight line between them, following the tester maker's instructions for the distances. I take a reading, then move the potential spike a little nearer and a little further away and read again. If the three readings agree closely, the result can be trusted; if not, I move the current spike further out and repeat. I record the readings, the spike distances, the date, the weather and soil condition, and the tester used. I compare the result with the value in the specification. Finally I reconnect the earthing conductor, check it is tight, and only then is the supply restored.
markingPoints: Isolates the installation and disconnects the earth conductor from the rod
Places current and potential spikes in line as the maker says
Takes readings at three positions and checks they agree
Records readings, distances, conditions and instrument; compares with the specification
Reconnects the earth conductor before the supply is restored

essays.stem: A 24 V AC control circuit on a training panel has a supply, a stop button, a start button and a contactor coil in series. The coil does not pull in. Explain how you would use a voltmeter to find the fault, step by step.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the meter on a known source and set it to AC volts. I measure the 24 V supply at its terminals to prove it is there. Then I keep the common (return) probe on the supply's return terminal and move the other probe along the circuit, one point at a time: after the stop button, after the start button while it is pressed, and at the coil terminal. At each point I should see about 24 V. Where the voltage disappears, the fault is between that point and the last good one, for example a stop button contact that does not close or a broken wire. If I see 24 V at the coil but it does not pull in, I check the coil's return connection and then isolate and measure the coil's resistance. Once the fault is found, I isolate, repair, test again and record what was wrong and what I did.
markingPoints: Checks the meter and the 24 V supply first
Keeps one probe on the return and moves the other along the circuit
Explains that the fault is where the voltage disappears
Checks the coil and its return, isolating before resistance tests
Repairs, retests and records

essays.stem: As team leader, explain how you would set up a system to keep the team's test instruments accurate and safe to use.
essays.modelAnswer: I would make a register of every instrument, with its serial number, type, owner, calibration date and the date the next calibration is due. Each instrument would carry a label showing its due date. Instruments would be sent for calibration at the interval the maker or the company sets, and any that are dropped, damaged or give odd readings would be sent sooner. Between calibrations, the team would check testers on a check box or against a reference meter, for example each week, and write the results in a log. Anyone using a tester must check it on a proving unit before and after use. Leads and probes would be inspected before each use, and damaged ones taken out of service at once. Instruments would be stored clean and dry in their cases, with spare batteries and the right fuses. Any results taken with an instrument found to be faulty would be checked again.
markingPoints: Register with serial numbers and due dates; labels on instruments
Calibration at set intervals and after damage
Regular checks against a check box or reference, with a log
Daily checks: proving units, leads and probes; faulty items withdrawn
Proper storage, and rechecking results from a faulty instrument

essays.stem: After testing a small shop's installation, one circuit has a low insulation reading and another has no RCD. Explain what your test report should contain and how you would deal with these two findings.
essays.modelAnswer: The report should give the customer's name and address, the date, who did the tests, the instruments used with their serial numbers and calibration dates, and what was tested. It should include the schedule of test results for every circuit, with the readings and whether each passed. The findings should be listed clearly with how urgent each one is. The circuit with a low insulation reading is a danger, so I would leave it isolated, locked off and labelled, explain to the customer why, and recommend finding and repairing the fault before it is used. The missing RCD would be listed as a recommendation to improve safety, especially for outlets used for portable equipment or in wet areas, with a note of the risk if it is not fitted. I would sign the report, keep a copy, and give the customer a quotation for the repairs.
markingPoints: Report details: customer, date, tester, instruments and calibration
Schedule of results with pass or fail for each circuit
Low insulation circuit left isolated, labelled and explained
Missing RCD recorded as a recommendation with its risk
Report signed, copy kept, customer advised on repairs

practical1.title: Inspect and dead-test a three-circuit training board, and complete a test schedule
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training board with a small distribution board and three final circuits (lighting, 110 V outlets and a 220 V outlet), wired but NOT connected to any supply. Some faults have been planted. As a group, plan the test order and give each member a role: test leader, tester, recorder and checker (members swap roles for each circuit, so everyone tests). Prove the board dead with a two-pole tester checked on a proving unit before and after. Check every instrument on the check box first. Then inspect the board, and test continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance (at the voltage the assessor sets, with any electronics disconnected) and polarity on every circuit. Record every reading on the schedule of test results, find each fault, and write a short report that lists the faults and what should be done. Do not repair the faults unless the assessor asks.
materials: Training board with distribution board and three circuits, not connected to any supply, with planted faults
Two-pole voltage indicator and proving unit
Insulation and continuity tester, with a check box of known resistances
Lock-off kit, tags and a padlock for each member
Blank schedule of test results and report sheet
photos: The group's written test plan with roles
The voltage indicator being checked on the proving unit before and after the test for dead
The tester being checked on the check box
A continuity test of a protective conductor at the far end of a circuit
An insulation test in progress, with switches closed
The completed schedule of test results
The finished report listing faults and actions
checklist: Took part in planning and kept to their role
Proved the board dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Checked the instrument on the check box and nulled the leads
Carried out at least one continuity, one insulation and one polarity test correctly
Recorded readings accurately against the right circuit
Found at least one planted fault and explained the evidence for it
Checked another member's readings and signed the schedule
Left the board and tools safe and tidy
safety: The board is never connected to a supply during this task
Prove dead with a checked two-pole tester before touching any terminal
Warn others before an insulation test, and let the circuit discharge before touching it
Use only leads and probes in good condition

practical2.title: Verify the group's instruments and compare current measurements on a low-voltage bench
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a bench with a 12 V DC bench supply, a set of known resistors (for example 1 Ω, 100 Ω, 10 kΩ and 1 MΩ) and a 24 V AC safety transformer feeding a resistive load of a few amps through a looped test lead. As a group, check each meter the group uses against the reference meter and the known resistors, and complete a verification log: the value applied, each meter's reading, the difference, and whether it is within the maker's stated accuracy. Each member checks at least one instrument. Then measure the current in the 24 V load three ways: with a meter in series (the assessor breaks the circuit when it is dead), with a clamp meter around one conductor, and with the conductor wound five times through the clamp. Compare the results, work out the percentage differences, and show that clamping both conductors together reads nearly zero. Present the log and your findings to the assessor.
materials: 12 V DC bench power supply and a 24 V AC safety transformer with a resistive load (set up by the assessor)
Reference meter and a set of known resistors
The group's multimeters, clamp meter and insulation and continuity tester
Looped test lead for the clamp meter
Maker's accuracy figures for each instrument
photos: The bench set-up, with the reference meter labelled
A meter being checked against a known resistor
The series ammeter reading on the 24 V load
The clamp meter around one conductor, then with five turns
The clamp around both conductors reading nearly zero
The completed verification log with differences worked out
checklist: Set each meter to the right function and range before connecting
Took readings accurately and wrote them down at once
Worked out each difference and compared it with the maker's accuracy
Used the clamp meter correctly, around one conductor only
Explained why five turns multiply the reading and why both conductors read nearly zero
Made changes to the circuit only with the supply off
Took part in presenting the findings
safety: Only the assessor connects the bench supplies; nothing above 24 V is used
